reason: Lay the prepared tracks over the soft drift to spread the wheels' load.
expectation: The tracks should create a firmer surface for crossing, though they may need anchoring.

alternatives.reason: The winch could help secure or pull the rover, but the track surface seems the first need.

effect: The tracks made the crossing; the remaining winch action may secure the rover for the crossing.
reaction: A sensible result, though I am curious how the winch is used.
reason: Attach the winch to the rock anchor; it is the only remaining combination and should help with the crossing.
expectation: I expect the winch to provide an anchored pull or safety line across the drift.

effect: The winch made an anchored recovery line, which can now be used with the crossing.
reaction: That matches my expectation and makes the recovery purpose clearer.
reason: Combine the line and crossing to get the rover safely over; it is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the rover to cross the drift with the line available for support or recovery.

effect: The combined line and crossing completed the route to the ice face.
reaction: It is satisfying to finish a practical construction, though the result gives little detail about the actual crossing.

mostWorthwhile.text: Laying the gravel-filled tracks was the most worthwhile action: it directly applied the load-spreading idea to the obstacle.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final combination felt rather terse: a secured crossing appeared without a description of how the line and tracks worked together.

surprise.text: Nothing especially surprised me; the recovery line and crossing were broadly what I expected.

arbitrary.text: Combining the recovery line with the gravel crossing made general sense, but the specific physical connection was unclear.

continue.text: I would continue to see what the protected ice contains; this brief crossing was purposeful but offered little discovery on its own.
